Reading skill

Recognise a text's purpose and layout

Decide whether a text informs, instructs, warns, invites or asks before you search for detail.

Official sources checked: 2026-09-19

Start with the source

Ask where the text would appear: a shop, workplace, school, health service, council office or phone screen. The setting narrows the likely purpose.

Read the largest clues

Headings, logos, bold words, dates, prices and action verbs reveal structure quickly. Use them before reading every line.

01PURPOSE02CLUE03EVIDENCE04ANSWER

Name the reader's action

A useful purpose statement says what the reader should know or do, such as attend an appointment, keep an area clear or return a form.

Check purpose against detail

A heading can attract attention, but the body controls the exact meaning. Confirm the purpose with at least one supporting detail.
